messages:
morgan: thinking through the migration plan — can we land a single gateway that accepts both JSON REST and gRPC (protobuf) clients and does safe fallbacks for tenants that can't upgrade their clients quickly? :thinking_face:

lena: in practice we do that with a translator layer. envoy + grpc-json-transcoder is the obvious path but watch out for schema edges (oneof, maps).

sam: agree. also need a clear contract for versioning. my suggestion: proto = source of truth, gateway exposes JSON that maps 1:1 to proto fields. if new required fields get added, gateway should provide defaults for JSON clients.

taylor: +1. we should also emit telemetry for any field-mismatch / unknown-field events so product teams can see who is hitting old clients. add a metric: api.migration.unknown_fields.count with labels {service, tenant}.

morgan: good call on telemetry. how do we handle streaming / bidi cases? some clients rely on streaming grpc for low-latency traces.

lena: streaming is harder. we can support unary forwarding for JSON via long-poll or SSE, but for full bidi best to require gRPC. we should document fallback semantics clearly in the console so customers know tradeoffs.

sam: operationally, fallback routing: prefer native endpoint (proto/gRPC) -> if not available or latch set on tenant, route to translator instance pool. translator pool must be autoscaled and circuit-breakered.

anya: question: do we want to mutate payloads server-side to insert defaults? sounds risky for audits. prefer to return structured validation error with a stable error code and automatic upgrade hints in the header.

taylor: +1 on not mutating. but we can supply a "compatibility-mode" header that promises the gateway will synthesize small fields (non-sensitive) for a short deprecation window. that should be behind an opt-in flag per tenant.

morgan: proto example I had in mind:
```proto
message CreateJobReq {
  string name = 1;
  repeated string tags = 2;
  oneof schedule {
    string cron = 3;
    google.protobuf.Timestamp at = 4;
  }
}
```
When JSON client omits schedule, gateway could set cron = "@hourly" if tenant opted into compat.

lena: if we do synth defaults we MUST log them as part of the request trace. otherwise debugging sucks. put a field in trace: request.metadata.generated_defaults = ["schedule.cron"].

sam: quota/ratelimiting implications: translator adds CPU/memory cost. we should bill translator invocations separately or tag them in cost telemetry so finance can analyze. add header X-Redwood-Translator: true.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary for "gateway-transcode-v2" finished — 3% traffic in prod, 0 errors in 2h. :white_check_mark:

anya: nice. can we wire the rollout UX so product teams can opt a tenant into translator via the console? small checkbox: "enable REST compatibility" with an expire date.

morgan: yes — console needs UI + audit trail + ability to bulk opt/rollback. UX note: default to OFF for new tenants.

taylor: also add a per-route telemetry view: % of requests translated, median latency delta, unknown_fields rate. put it on model/route dashboard.

lena: implementation notes: keep proto as canonical. store mapping docs in repo alongside protos (md with examples). use integration tests that exercise both proto and JSON permutations.

sam: for rollout safety: canary -> tenant opt-in -> automated A/B comparing quality (0-downgrade tolerance). if quality regressions spike, auto-disable translator for that tenant and notify SE.

morgan: sounds like a plan. action items: 1) infra: translator pool with circuit breaker + header tagging (sam) 2) console: opt-in checkbox + audit log (anya) 3) telemetry: generated_defaults metric, translated_requests, latency_delta (taylor) 4) docs + integration tests (lena).

anya: I'll add console mockups to the shared Figma and link in a follow-up.

morgan: thanks — let's sync tomorrow after canary window. :thumbsup:
